- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 10–15% below true peak.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.30) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; add 2–5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price by 2–5% when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; apply small upward bias.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive days of price decline), model often fails to adjust; add 1–3% upward bias to counteract lag.  
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed, model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.
